subject: Accountancy
central_question: How are accrual-based adjustments incorporated at two places in final accounts so that profit and financial position present a true and fair view?
in_scope_units: Need for adjustments under the accrual basis.
Accrued income and income received in advance.
Bad debts and further bad debts.
Manager's commission before or after charging commission.
Preparation of adjusted trading and profit and loss account and balance sheet.
banned_topics: Simple final accounts without adjustments, which belong to Financial Statements – I.
Detailed depreciation methods and asset disposal, which belong to Chapter 7.
Trial-balance rectification and suspense account, which belong to Chapter 6.

known_pitfalls.claim: An adjustment is shown only in the profit and loss account.
known_pitfalls.correction: Every adjustment has a double effect and normally appears at two places in final accounts.

known_pitfalls.claim: Outstanding expense is deducted from the expense.
known_pitfalls.correction: It is added to the expense and shown as a current liability.

known_pitfalls.claim: Prepaid expense is added to the current expense.
known_pitfalls.correction: It is deducted from expense and shown as a current asset.

known_pitfalls.claim: The provision percentage is applied before writing off further bad debts.
known_pitfalls.correction: Further bad debts are deducted from debtors first; the provision is calculated on the remaining balance.

known_pitfalls.claim: Manager's commission formula is the same whether profit is before or after commission.
known_pitfalls.correction: Commission on profit after charging commission requires a denominator of 100 plus the rate.

recommended_example_progression: Use Ankit's trial balance and closing stock ₹15,000 to show the first two-place adjustment.
Use outstanding wages ₹500, prepaid salary ₹5,000, accrued commission ₹1,500 and rent received in advance ₹3,000 to practise accrual adjustments.
Use furniture depreciation ₹1,500 and further bad debts ₹2,500 to revise non-cash and debtor adjustments.
Use the chapter's provision and manager's commission illustrations to calculate revised expenses and liabilities.
Use the comprehensive Shri R. Lal illustration and end questions to prepare complete adjusted final accounts.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with Short Answer Questions, Long Answer Questions and comprehensive numerical problems on adjusted final accounts, including provisions and manager's commission.
